segments.name: Operations/customer success lead at a fast-growing company
segments.organization: Scaling SaaS or service company with a dedicated ops/CS function
segments.workflow: Builds and maintains customer-facing intake forms (support triage, satisfaction surveys, onboarding) that route into team tools, replacing ad hoc spreadsheets or email threads; multiple teammates need to edit and brand these forms under one shared workspace
segments.need: Run structured, branded, team-maintained customer-facing forms/surveys that integrate into existing workflow tools (e.g. Notion, Google Sheets, Make, Zapier) without engineering help
segments.buyer_role: Ops or CS team lead / manager who controls the team's tool budget
segments.user_role: Operations/customer success team members who build and edit forms collaboratively
segments.current_alternative: Spreadsheets, email-based intake, Typeform, or Google Forms with manual routing

reasons: Fetched examples (GLOWDEGA, Handl.me) show a solo skincare-studio owner and a niche community founder using branded client-intake/user-research forms, not the described scaling SaaS/service company with a dedicated multi-person ops/CS function editing shared forms

Pro's collaboration, custom-domain and branding-removal features (tally.so/pricing) technically match the stated need, but no fetched source shows a company with a dedicated ops/CS team and multiple form editors actually running or paying for this workflow at the scale the candidate describes
Re-ranked on matching researched sources (3 fetched).
unknowns: Whether any organization with a dedicated, multi-person ops/CS function and shared form editing actually uses Tally this way, versus the solo/small-team examples that were fetched
Whether the free tier's unlimited forms/submissions already satisfies this audience, removing the stated Pro-upgrade trigger

evidence.claim: A solo client-facing business (not a scaling ops/CS team) used Tally for operational customer intake, showing the form-type fits the workflow but not the described team size
evidence.quote: "Before Tally," she says, "we saw a major drop-off partway through our intake questionnaire—it was just too long. Now, clients see the questions relevant to them based on previous answers."

evidence.claim: A niche community founder values brand-consistent, co-branded forms, illustrating demand for branding/custom-domain features but at a small-organization scale, not an ops/CS department
evidence.quote: I really dislike sending external tools that don't reflect our brand. I want everything we send to feel like it's coming straight from us [...] This also allows us to strengthen our brand and collaborate with other federations where we might need to use purpose-designed visuals inside the forms to showcase our partnership.

evidence.claim: Pro plan explicitly offers the multi-editor collaboration capability this audience would need, confirming product compatibility if such a team exists
evidence.quote: Collaboration. Invite unlimited team members to shared workspaces.

segments.who: Operations or customer success leads/managers at growing companies who need shared, branded customer-facing forms
segments.why_them: They already run customer-facing processes at volume (e.g. hundreds of queries/day) and need team-editable, de-branded forms wired into existing stacks like Notion/Sheets/Make
pains: Spreadsheet/email-based intake doesn't scale with query volume
Free-tier branding and lack of custom domain look unprofessional for customer-facing forms
Multiple teammates need to co-edit forms, which free single-user setups don't support well
segments.objection: Why pay for Pro when the free tier already offers unlimited forms and submissions?
segments.basis: Grounded in Make.com's documented 300-queries/day Tally use case (Zapier blog) and Tally's own Pro-tier feature list (collaboration, custom domain, branding removal) as the plausible upgrade trigger; the specific buying trigger and whether Make.com itself pays for Pro is unverified.

segments.name: Independent creator or solo entrepreneur
segments.organization: Solo-run product, newsletter, or small SaaS/creator business
segments.workflow: Builds lightweight feedback, waitlist, or lead-gen forms directly, often no-code, to collect input from users/subscribers and feed it into a personal workflow (email list, Notion, Sheets)
segments.need: Collect product feedback, waitlist signups, or leads cheaply and quickly without hiring a developer or paying for enterprise-grade survey tools
segments.buyer_role: The founder/creator themselves, who is also the sole user and payer
segments.current_alternative: Typeform (seen as expensive/limited free tier), Google Forms (seen as unpolished), or no formal form at all

reasons: Two Indie Hackers threads show solo founders explicitly rejecting Typeform's pricing/response caps as a trigger, and in one case the founder states in first person that he signed up for Tally as a direct result

Tally's pricing page confirms the free tier's unlimited forms/submissions match this audience's lightweight feedback/waitlist/lead-gen workflow, supporting compatibility without requiring any paid capability
unknowns: Whether these founders (or similar solo operators) ever moved past free-tier use to a paid plan, given the pricing page's free unlimited forms/submissions claim
Whether 2020-2021 Indie Hackers sentiment toward Tally as the standard Typeform alternative still holds against newer competitors in 2026
No product requirement is mapped for this audience, so compatibility is unchecked rather than doubtful.

evidence.claim: A second solo operator independently names response caps and ugly free alternatives (Google Forms) as the pain driving a search for a Typeform alternative, corroborating the first thread
evidence.quote: The pricing with a cap on responses per month feels like it's only designed to make you pay more and to pay $59 a month immediately. I've been using google forms which is fine but it's pretty ugly.

evidence.claim: Indie Hackers threads function as a concrete, publicly accessible venue where solo founders ask for and receive form-builder recommendations, including Tally by name
evidence.quote: <https://tally.so/> is popular here

segments.who: Solo founders, indie developers, and small creators building forms for feedback, waitlists, or lead capture
segments.why_them: They are explicitly, publicly comparison-shopping form builders against Typeform on cost/limits grounds, and Tally is repeatedly recommended as the answer in that exact conversation
pains: Typeform's free tier caps responses and paywalls conditional logic
Needs a professional-looking form without hiring a developer
Budget-constrained; unwilling to pay enterprise survey pricing

segments.basis: Grounded in Indie Hackers forum threads where users explicitly ask for Typeform alternatives and Tally is named as the standard answer; free-tier sufficiency is a known counterevidence limiting paid conversion likelihood.

dossier.audience_name: Operations/customer success lead at a fast-growing company
dossier.orientation: Tally is a no-code form builder whose paid plan lets an ops/CS team maintain shared, unbranded customer-facing forms on their own subdomain and route submissions into other work tools.

setup_conditions: Pro plan subscription (€20/month or $29/month) is required for branding removal, custom domains and shared-workspace collaboration
Point the custom (sub)domain at Tally to produce branded form links
Connect the form to downstream tools through the documented Zapier integration
decision_gaps: Does Tally publish native connectors for Notion, Google Sheets and Make, and which field or property types do they not support?
Does Tally document role-based permissions in shared workspaces, given the help docs state all organization members have the same create/edit/delete rights?
defining_need_fit.supported_core_workflow: Run structured, branded, team-maintained customer-facing forms/surveys that integrate into existing workflow tools (e.g. Notion, Google Sheets, Make, Zapier) without engineering help
defining_need_fit.caveat: Integration is licensed here only through the Zapier path to 2,000+ apps and the API; native Notion, Google Sheets and Make connectors are not established by the selected evidence, and the named tools are examples rather than a required all-native guarantee.
defining_need_fit.why: The documented no-code/AI form building, unlimited-member shared workspaces, branding removal, custom (sub)domain hosting and Zapier routing together cover the stated task on the Pro plan.

ranked_relevance.why: Unlimited team members in shared workspaces is the documented mechanism for the required multiple-editor, team-maintained form.
Removing Tally branding is a required capability in the audience definition for branded customer-facing forms.
Custom (sub)domain hosting is the second required capability, producing branded links for customer-facing intake.
Zapier connection to 2,000+ apps is the licensed mechanism for routing submissions into existing workflow tools without engineering help.
Plain-language generation and editing describes how non-engineers build and change these forms.
Unlimited forms and submissions within fair usage supports an ordinary-volume evaluation before paying.
Same free-tier scope stated on the features page, with the fair-usage condition preserved.
€20/month Pro is the price of the plan carrying the two required branding capabilities and collaboration.
$29/month or $290/year with cancel-anytime is the alternative currency statement of the same required plan.
30-day version restore is a documented safeguard for forms several teammates edit in production.
90-day restore on Business extends that safeguard for longer-lived production intake forms.
Scheduled submission deletion is relevant to customer data collected through support and satisfaction forms, on Business only.
API create/update/delete is the documented secondary integration route when a connector is unavailable.
File collection matters for support triage attachments, bounded by the 10MB free-plan limit.
Stripe checkout forms are true and licensed but outside this audience's intake and survey workflow.
Email verification is framed as lead quality and conversion, not the stated support or satisfaction workflow.
Removing the per-file upload cap is not a researched requirement for this segment.
Duplicate statement of the same upload-limit removal; adds nothing for this need.
Redundant with E19 on Pro version history and weaker for selection.
The Claude connector is not established as part of this audience's stack by the audience evidence.
Business pricing is only relevant if retention or email verification is required, which is unestablished here.
Same Business tier in dollars; premature for a first decision at the Pro requirement level.
A solo creator's feedback-campaign response rate is not a description of the mechanism this team needs, and its scope is that single campaign.
Unattributed company-wide team count with no methodology; background only and not licensed as proof.
